summary: The Republic of the Marshall Islands' ecosystem pledges are exclusively conservation-oriented. The Challenge sought to conserve at least 30% of near-shore marine resources and 20% of terrestrial resources across Micronesia by 2020. Leaders including RMI subsequently affirmed the new Micronesia Challenge 2030, with collective goals to manage at least 50% of marine resources and 30% of terrestrial resources. In 2025, the government established the Bikar and Bokak national sanctuaries, protecting around 48,000 km² of ocean and atolls. This marine area is about 197.5 times the country's reported 243 km² total land area; the geographical context records 217 km² of water, or 89.4% of the country. The supplied non-water classes total 24 km²—13 km² of agriculture and 11 km² of sparse vegetation. Because the percentage targets are regional rather than country-specific, they are not direct percentages of national land-cover shares.
